full_judgment:
SM Hossain J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon respondent Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the two minors, namely (1) Sagorika Noami Azad Huq and. (2) Mehrab Faraj Huq, daughter and son respectively of the petitioner, should not be brought before this Court so as to satisfy itself that the said minors are not being held in custody without lawful authority or in an unlawful manner by respondent Nos. 1.3. 

 The petitioner, was given in marriage to respondent No.1 on 15-1-1993. The petitioner was always subjected to torture and oppression and was in continuous physiological pressure. Two minors were born to the petitioner, a daughter, Sagorika Noami Azad Huq on 30-8-2000 and a .son, Mehrab Faraj Huq on 11-12-2002. The petitioner in  the absence of her husband, respondent No. 1 who was in USA from 4th  February 2005 was regularly tortured by respondent Nos. 2 and 3. Though the petitioner was tortured regularly but for the sake of her two minor children, she could not take any steps to come out of the marital life. Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 who are not thinking about the children and their welfare compelled respondent No.1 to divorce the petitioner on 23-4-2006. At this stage, respondent Nos. 2 and 3 played a dubious role and surreptitiously kept her in their house for 90 days, assuring that they would bring about reconciliation in respect of the divorce, between her and respondent No.1. After expiry of 90 days of divorce, respondent Nos. 2 and 3 invited the petitioner's two brothers and imputed various false accusations and allegations against the petitioner and in that traumatic situation, they forced her and her two brothers to put signature on some blank stamp papers and threw her out of the house forcibly, detaining her two minor children. The petitioner came to the house of her mother, who had been suffering from various diseases including cancer. The petitioner started living with her mother and she could not do anything for bringing her minor children, who were kept in the unlawful custody of respondent Nos. 2 and 3. The petitioner tried several times to visit her minor children but was not allowed more than two times within 8 months. Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 always dropped the telephone calls made by the petitioner, who was not allowed to have free access to see her children. For the sake of welfare and security of the two minor children, the right of custody (hizanat) lies with the mother according to Muslim Law till they attain certain age. But in this case, the two minors have been deprived of their mother's love and custody. On 29-1-07, the petitioner came to know that respondent No. 1 came back to Bangladesh from USA with a new wife and that they were going to hold a wedding reception on 1 February 2007. The petitioner also came to know that she could not have access to the two minors because respondent Nos. 2 and 3 had used the forged signed stamp paper as a "deed of handing over the two minor children of the petitioner to respondent Nos. 2 and 3". The petitioner also came to know that her, two minor children would be soon taken by respondent No. 1 along with his newly married wife to USA. The petitioner apprehends that she will not be able to see and take care of her minor children who would be deprived of their mother's love, care and affection. The petitioner, therefore, went to Gulshan Police Station and lodged two GD entries. The petitioner filed Family Case No. 61 of 2007 in the 5th Court of Assistant Judge Dhaka for the custody of her two minor children. The petitioner does not know when the case will be finalised and the threat of taking away the two minor children from Bangladesh to USA in violation of their mother's custodial right exists to live in agony with the stepmother who cannot ensure the welfare of the children. The petitioner further feels that she will not be able to do anything for her minor children if they are taken abroad out of their mother's legal custody. 

 3. Finding no other efficacious and alternative remedy, the petitioner had to file this writ petition under Article 102(1)(b)(2) of the Constitution. A Division Bench of this Court issued Rule Nisi on 5-2-2007. 

 4. Respondent Nos. 1-3 filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting all the material allegations made in the writ petition. Their case, in short, is that to have a right enforced through Court, a person ought to have come to the Court with clean hands. A mother has a legal right to have the custody of the minor children but that legal right is not always exercisable, more particularly when the mother is guilty of immoral activities. The welfare of the children is to be looked into by this Court prior to adjudicating the matter between the contesting parties to have the custody of a minor boy and a minor girl. The ultimate welfare will play a great role to adjudicate upon the present issue and moreover, when the mother accepted the divorce by her husband for immoral activities during their marital tie. The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 and the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985 are there to deal with the matter of custody and guardianship of minor children. Upon invoking the said jurisdiction, the petitioner has already filed Family Suit No. 61 of 2007 in the 5th Court of Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court, Dhaka. As the petitioner invoked the appropriate jurisdiction; she has no legal right to raise the same issue subsequently before this Court and therefore, the, writ petition is not maintainable. The respondents are respectively the father and the paternal grand parents of the minor children and, as such, the writ of habeas corpus is not maintainable in the given facts and circumstances against the respondents who are the legal guardian of the minors. Respondent No.3 is a fully retired professor and grandmother of the minors and she personally accompanies the minors to and from the school and passes her whole time with the minors. Respondent No.2 is a retired educationist of excellence and he passes full time with the minors. The respondents assure and undertake that the minors would not be taken out of the country and the petitioner will be allowed to visit at agreed time and place without any hindrance till the matter of custody is decided by the Family Court upon taking evidence as to the welfare of the minors. It is totally untrue that the petitioner was ever tortured or was put under any pressure physiological or otherwise by anyone. She was always taken care of and all her wishes were fulfilled. The luxurious lifestyle that the petitioner enjoyed could be possible because of full support and affection of respondent Nos. 2 and 3. Respondent No. 1 is a graduate in Computer Science from the Minnesota University of , USA: On his return to Bangladesh in 1990, he initially worked in the BRAC, and the Bangladesh Computer Council as a consultant. He made reputation in his profession and in 1992 established his own company, the Pradeshta Limited. He was always research minded and he became the pioneer of introducing E-mail services in Bangladesh in 1993. Considering the importance of technology the US AID Agency decided to introduce him to the USA market and arranged for his visit to Washington DC. On February 4, 2005, respondent No. 1 left for USA to file application for the USA patent. While in USA, respondent No. 1 on enquiry came to know that the petitioner was spending time with old and new boy friends in restaurants and parks leaving the children in the care of others. Respondent  No. 1 then came to learn from reliable sources. based on irrefutable evidence that the petitioner established illicit relationship, with a lover whom she was meeting regularly. Through his reliable agent, respondent No.1 arranged tape recording of obnoxious telephone conversations for several days. Respondent No. 1 rushed from USA to Dhaka and made further enquiry about the situation. When satisfied about illicit relationship he had no other alternative but to divorce the petitioner according to Muslim Law on 23-4-2006 on the ground of infidelity. In the facts and circumstances of the present case and in view of her illicit relationship.and her present lifestyle, the petitioner is not the proper person for custody of the minors. The respondents also filed a supplementary affidavit stating that they made all attempts to settle the .matter amicably but failed to do so because of intransigence of the petitioner. 

 5. Ms Fauzia Karim Firoz, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner is entitled to the custody of her two, minor children till the question of custody is otherwise adjudicated by a competent Court and that till then she has the absolute right to have the custody of her minor children. She further submits that until the question of custody is adjudicated, the custody of the minor children cannot be with the respondents and that the settled principle of law could not be ignored. 

 6. Mr Mohammad Ozair Farooq, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent Nos. 1-3, on the other hand, submits that the present writ petition is not maintainable against respondent Nos. 1-3 and that the question of custody will betaken care of by the Family Court where the petitioner filed Family Case No. 61 of 2007. He further submits that on the facts and in the circumstances of the instant case, the mother, cannot have the custody of her minor children because of her illicit relationship with an unknown person. He lastly submits that till the question of custody is adjudicated by a competent Court, the respondents should be allowed to have the custody of the minors. He lastly submits that the present writ petition is misconceived and not maintainable as the minors are not in the custody of respondent Nos. 2 and 3 without lawful authority or in an unlawful manner. 

 7. We have perused the writ petition, its annexures and the affidavit-in-opposition and the supplementary affidavit and its annexures. Admittedly the petitioner was given in marriage to respondent No. 1 on 15-1-1993. Out of their wedlock a son and a daughter were born. Daughter Sagorika Noami Azad Huq was born on 30-8-2000 and son Mehrab Faraj Huq on 11-12-2002. In deciding the question of custody of the minor children the paramount consideration before the Court is welfare of the minors. The term welfare must be read in the largest possible sense which means that every circumstance must be taken into consideration and the Court must do what under the circumstances a wise paren acting for the true interests of the child would do or ought to do. It is difficult for us in the habeas corpus petition to take evidence without which the question as to what is the interest of the child cannot satisfactorily be determined. the petitioner already filed Family Case No. 61 of 2007 in the 5th, Court of Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court, Dhaka under section 25(1) of Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 and the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985 praying for custody of her minor children. It is contended by the respondents that since the mother is leading an immoral life, she should not be allowed the custody of the minor children and her previous conduct shows that she cannot look after the affairs of the minors and that having been divorced by respondent No.1, she would not be able to maintain the children. As already stated the question of welfare of the children will be adjudicated by the Family Court, taking into consideration the relevant facts and the circumstances and the evidence necessary for the disposal of that case. In this connection it is pertinent to quote from DF Mullah about the right of mother to custody of infant children as under: 

 The mother is entitled to the custody (hizanat) of her male child until he has completed the age of seyen years ,and of her female child until she has attained puberty. The right continues though she is divorced by the father of the child unless she marries a second husband in which case the custody belongs to the father". Till the custody of the minors is decided by a competent Court, mother is legally entitled to retain the custody of her minor children. Before adjudication of the custody of the minors by competent Court if they remain in the custody of anybody other than the mother, that custody will be without lawful authority. The Family Court will take care of all aspects of the case and will come to a definite finding as to who is/are entitled to the custody of the minors taking into consideration the paramount question of welfare of the minors but till then the minors shall remain in the custody of the mother as provided under the law. In this connection reliance may be placed on the case of Abdul Jalil and others vs Sharon Laily Begum Jalil 1998 BLD (AD) 21 =50 DLR (AD) 55. The case referred to is almost identical with the facts and circumstances of the instant case where the legal fight was between the father and the divorced mother over the custody of their minor children. In that case although senous allegations, including illicit relationship with a man, were leveiled against the mother, the Appellate Division found that till final adjudication of the question of guardianship by the Family Court, the custody of the minors would remain with the mother. Since the above case fits in with the facts and circumstances of the instant case, we do not have any other option but to rely on the principle enunciated in that case. 

 10. Regarding maintainability of the writ petition it appears that the case reported in 1998 BLD (AD) 21 arises out of a habeas corpus petition filed before the High Court Division. 

 "But then we find substance in the submission of Dr Hossain that normally the minor children should be with their mother as long as she does not earn any disqualification for such custody and if there is a breach of this normal order brought about by an unilateral act of the father or anybody on his behalf, the aggrieved mother has the right to move the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution for immediate custody of the children which may be ordered in, the interest and for the welfare of the said children" 

 14. The respondents shall have the liberty to see the minors twice in a week at the residence of the petitioner or at a place to be agreed upon between the parties. If any dispute (seeing the minors) arises in this regard it will be taken care of by the family Court. 

 16. The 5th Court of Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court is directed to dispose of Family Case No.61 of 2007 within 3(three) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment. The findings of this Court shall have no bearing on the Family Court Case. Let a copy of the judgment be sent to the 5th Court of Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court, Dhaka in connection with Family Case No. 61 of 2007 by a special messenger of this Court at the cost of the petitioner.
